title: AUK Analytics PoC benchmarking playbook: latency, throughput & cost
content:
Executive summary:

This doc captures the results and playbook from the AUK Analytics PoC benchmarking and the 2029-11-13 workshop. Goal: provide a repeatable evaluation matrix that ties p95/p99 latency, end-to-end QPS, and per-token cost to deployment choices (GPU family, instance shape, batching, quantization, warmup). Outcome: two practical deployment recommendations (one low-latency, one cost-optimized) plus short-term mitigations for observed tail-latency microbursts.

High-level findings (top-line):
- Low-latency config (single H100/80GB, dynamic batching max_batch=8, KV cache warm) achieves p95=95–110ms and p99=220–280ms for the sample chat workload at steady-state (1.2–1.5k tokens/s).
- Cost-optimized config (A100 multi-gpu pool with int8 quantized model + aggressive batching max_batch=32) yields 3–3.5x lower per-token cost but p95 increases to 240–320ms and p99 to 650–900ms at similar token throughput.
- Cold-starts and cache-warmup dominate the outliers: cold first-token latencies were 1.1–1.6s (single-GPU) and 1.6–2.4s (shared multi-tenant pool) depending on model variant and kernel precompilation state.
- Microburst tail events correlated with upstream request coalescing jitter on client side and with autoscaler scale-up windows (observed 8–18s window before additional pods accepted traffic).

Test matrix and workloads:
- Workloads used: 
  - Chat-simulated (multi-turn chat, avg 180 tokens per request, 4 concurrent requests per user simulation)
  - Single-turn summarization (avg 420 tokens)
  - Short-embedding batch (for throughput-only comparison)
- Models evaluated (PoC-provided + Redwood variants):
  - rw-base-13b-fp16 (baseline)
  - rw-opt-13b-int8 (aggressive quant)
  - rw-mistral-32b-8k (larger-model baseline)
  - rw-lite-7b-q4 (cheap/edge comparison)
- Hardware shapes: single-GPU H100-80GB, single GPU A100-80GB, 2x A100 pod (multi-gpu stripe), Dedicated pool (4 x A100) with autoscale policy.
- Key knobs: quantization (fp16, int8, q4), batching (max_batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16, 32), prefix/KV cache warmup policies, kernel-compile prewarm, request routing (dedicated vs hosted), autoscaler thresholds (cpu/gpu util and queue length).

Methodology notes (reproducibility):
- Runs executed from Redwood's benchmark harness (bench-runner v2.3). Scripts and seed corpora are in linked_artifacts (Confluence-5247).
- Each combination ran for 20 minutes after a 5 minute warmup; for steady-state numbers we used the final 10 minutes.
- For p99 we used the full-run aggregated percentiles across 10 runs. Cost approximations use Redwood’s cost model (token compute cost + GPU time amortized + networking), summarized as $ per 1M tokens.

Representative results (steady-state aggregated):
- rw-base-13b-fp16 on single H100, dynamic batch max=8:
  - QPS (requests/s): 45 (avg tokens/s: 1,350)
  - p50/p95/p99 (ms): 28 / 105 / 260
  - cost per 1M tokens: ~$62
- rw-opt-13b-int8 on 2x A100 pod, max_batch=32:
  - QPS: 130 (tokens/s: 3,900)
  - p50/p95/p99 (ms): 40 / 310 / 820
  - cost per 1M tokens: ~$18
- rw-mistral-32b-8k on single H100, max_batch=4:
  - QPS: 18 (tokens/s: 540)
  - p50/p95/p99 (ms): 52 / 140 / 360
  - cost per 1M tokens: ~$145
- rw-lite-7b-q4 on single A100, max_batch=16 (edge config):
  - QPS: 230 (tokens/s: 6,900)
  - p50/p95/p99 (ms): 18 / 85 / 210
  - cost per 1M tokens: ~$9

Observations and interpretation:
- Quantization (int8/q4) provides outsized cost benefits but increases variance and tail latency; this is likely due to fallback kernel paths and cache inefficiencies under larger batch sizes.
- For mid-size models (13b), single H100 deployments with small dynamic batch sizes give the cleanest tail behavior for interactive chat workloads.
- Multi-gpu pooling (shared multi-tenant A100 pool) is attractive for throughput and unit economics but requires careful autoscaler tuning and request shaping to avoid 500–900ms p99 spikes during brief scale events.
- KV cache warmup policy: explicit client-side warmup (pre-warm frequent prefixes or pin sessions) reduced p99 by ~35% in samples; recommend session affinity where possible.

Workshop notes (2029-11-13, AUK engineering call):
- AUK priority = interactive analyst workflows (low-latency exploratory chat), secondary = bulk summarization batches at night (cost sensitive).
- AUK asked for a concrete starter: a single-H100 low-latency cluster (pinned model) + a secondary cost pool for nightly batch jobs.
- Discussed tradeoffs of model size vs responsiveness; AUK leaning to 13b family for now due to accuracy/latency sweet spot.
- Action item raised by Diego: measure cold-start delta across dedicated vs hosted (JIRA-SE-3248).

Recommendations (starter and scale):
1) Starter low-latency deployment (recommended for AUK immediate rollout):
   - Dedicated single-node H100, pinned model rw-base-13b-fp16, dynamic batching max_batch=8, precompile kernels at deploy time, session affinity + explicit cache-warm on login flows.
   - Autoscaler: scale by queue-length (threshold=4) and limit scale-up to 1 pod per 12s to avoid noisy neighbour spin.
   - Expected: p95 ~100ms, p99 <300ms at target QPS (target 40–60 rps).

2) Cost-optimized batch tier (nightly heavy jobs):
   - Dedicated A100 pool with rw-opt-13b-int8, large batch sizes (max_batch=32), aggressive multiplexing, spot instances if tolerable.
   - Schedule jobs into burst windows with warmup phase to amortize kernel compile.
   - Expected: ~3x lower per-token cost vs starter, acceptable p95/p99 for batched workflows.

Short-term mitigations for tail events:
- Implement client-side request jittering (randomized 5–20ms) to smooth coalescing spikes.
- Add a cold-start prewarm job after deploys and before business hours; run a short prefix corpus to reduce first-request penalties.
- Tune autoscaler to be quicker for scale-down but slightly conservative for scale-up (reduce simultaneous scale-up frequency).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: How does p99 change when serving mixed traffic (chat + embeddings) on same pool? (Diego assigned, due 2029-11-28)
- Q2: Can we reproduce the quantization-related tail in a kernel-instrumented run? (Liam assigned, due 2029-11-25)
- Q3: Explore session affinity mechanisms for hosted vs dedicated (Hannah assigned, due 2029-12-02).

Action items (owners & dates):
- Diego: Run dedicated vs hosted cold-start experiment (JIRA-SE-3248) — due 2029-11-28.
- Liam: Kernel-instrumented qint8 run and trace collection — due 2029-11-25.
- Hannah: Draft deployment runbook for starter flow and cache-warm strategy — due 2029-11-27.
- Priya: Prepare slide summary for AUK exec check-in (one pager) — due 2029-11-22.

- Confirm that rw-opt-13b-int8 binary uses the latest kernel pack from serving-runtime PR#1428.

- Bench command examples: bench-runner --config auk-chat-v1.yaml --model rw-base-13b-fp16 --hardware h100-single --duration 00:25:00 --warmup 00:05:00
